extracted.intended_audience: educational institutions, Title IX coordinators, compliance officers, K-12 and postsecondary administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and implementation guidance for how recipients must define, respond to, and adjudicate sexual harassment under Title IX, including the use and limits of supportive measures and grievance procedures in K-12 and postsecondary contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sexual harassment (§106.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual harassment is defined by three prongs: (1) conditioning the provision of an educational aid, benefit, or service on an individual's participation in unwelcome sexual conduct (quid pro quo); (2) unwelcome conduct on the basis of sex that a reasonable person would determine is so severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive that it effectively denies a person equal access to the recipient's education program or activity; and (3) sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, or stalking on the basis of sex as defined in the Clery Act and VAWA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The focus is on prohibited conduct irrespective of a person's sexual orientation or gender identity. Any individual may experience any of the three prongs. The Department will not tolerate sexual harassment as defined in §106.30 against any student, including LGBTQ students. The definition includes unwelcome conduct based on sex or sex stereotyping and is not limited to conduct of a sexual nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of phrase 'on the basis of sex' and decision not to define 'sex'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department incorporates the statutory phrase 'on the basis of sex' from Title IX and declines to define the word 'sex' in these final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word 'sex' is undefined in Title IX; defining it would have consequences beyond the scope of this rulemaking (e.g., athletics). The final regulations focus on prohibited conduct and will look to the Title IX statute and existing implementing regulations for the meaning of 'sex' for Title IX purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited to sex discrimination (sexual harassment) under Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations concern sexual harassment as a form of sex discrimination and do not address discrimination on the basis of race, disability, or other protected characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department lacks authority to promulgate regulations addressing non-sex protected characteristics under Title IX; other statutes (e.g., Title VI) govern those areas. Recipients should enforce other applicable statutes/regulations for non-sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures are individualized services that are non-disciplinary, non-punitive, designed to restore or preserve equal access to education, and that do not unreasonably burden the other party; they may include measures to protect safety of parties or the educational environment or deter sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures may be offered to complainants and respondents, free of charge. The Department revised the definition to insert 'equal' before 'access' and clarified the wording to state measures must be designed to restore or preserve equal access. The definition permits a wide range of individualized services and does not require listing specific measures in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to offer supportive measures to complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(a) requires recipients to offer supportive measures to every complainant irrespective of whether a formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must offer these measures as part of their non-deliberately indifferent response. The Department removed the proposed 'supportive measures safe harbor' and thus requires offering supportive measures in elementary and secondary schools as well as postsecondary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures must not unreasonably burden the other party
rubrics_metrics.description: A supportive measure cannot unreasonably burden the other party; whether a burden is 'unreasonable' is a fact-specific inquiry that depends on the educational programs, activities, opportunities, and benefits at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will not specify a list of what is 'unreasonable' because that would remove recipients' discretion to consider unique facts and circumstances. Examples: schedule/housing adjustments, removal from sports teams, or other restrictions may or may not be 'unreasonable' depending on context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures must be non-disciplinary and non-punitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures are defined to be non-disciplinary and non-punitive and therefore recipients are prohibited from imposing disciplinary sanctions or other non-supportive measures without following the §106.45 grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients' grievance procedures must describe the range of disciplinary sanctions they might impose following a determination of responsibility, and must describe the range of supportive measures available. Certain actions (suspension, expulsion, termination) are inherently disciplinary and cannot be supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction between listed disciplinary sanctions and supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient's grievance process lists a specific action (e.g., ineligibility to play on a sports team) as a possible disciplinary sanction, that action may not be taken as a supportive measure without following the §106.45 grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an action is not described as a disciplinary sanction in the recipient's process, whether it may be taken as a supportive measure depends on whether it is disciplinary/punitive or unreasonably burdensome in the particular facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation when supportive measures are not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient does not provide a complainant with supportive measures, the recipient must document the reasons why such a response was not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances under §106.45(b)(10)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates an accountability requirement for recipients who choose not to offer supportive measures in particular situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must conclude grievance processes within a reasonably prompt time frame
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient is obligated to conclude a grievance process within a reasonably prompt time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring prompt resolution limits the duration for which supportive measures maintain a status quo balancing of access while a grievance process is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removals and administrative leave permitted as interim actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a respondent poses an immediate threat to the physical health or safety of the complainant (or others), §106.44(c) allows emergency removals of respondents prior to the conclusion of a grievance process; non-student employees may be placed on administrative leave pursuant to §106.44(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removals are distinct from supportive measures and are authorized when immediate safety threats exist; recipients may also remove respondents from programs in emergency situations regardless of whether a grievance is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures after a finding of non-responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not require recipients to lift, remove, or cease supportive measures for complainants or respondents upon a finding of non-responsibility; recipients retain discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination of non-responsibility may reflect insufficient evidence rather than false allegations; recipients may continue measures because supportive measures are non-punitive and non-unreasonably burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures applicability and examples in elementary and secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Many common school actions to intervene and correct behavior (educational conversations, sending students to the principal's office, changing seating or class assignments) are not punitive or disciplinary and therefore do not violate the definition of supportive measures or §106.44(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By contrast, expulsions and suspensions are disciplinary and cannot be imposed without following a §106.45 grievance process. The regulations apply only to conduct that meets the sexual harassment definition in §106.30, not every instance of student misbehavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-specific analysis for removal from sports or extracurriculars
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether removal from sports teams or similar exclusions may be a supportive measure requires a fact-specific analysis; the unreasonableness of the burden does not depend solely on whether the respondent retains access to academic programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the action unreasonably burdens the respondent's access to the array of educational opportunities and benefits offered by the recipient. Some changes (e.g., schedule change) may more often be acceptable than excluding participation in extracurriculars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures obligations (§106.8 and §106.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt and publish grievance procedures that provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of complaints alleging any action that would be prohibited by Part 106, and must have a grievance process that complies with §106.45 for formal complaints of sexual harassment as defined in §106.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(c) clarifies that recipients do not need to use §106.45 for sex discrimination complaints that do not constitute sexual harassment. Recipient's non-discrimination statement, Title IX Coordinator designation, policy, grievance procedures, and training materials should be readily accessible pursuant to §106.8 and §106.45(b)(10)(i)(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibilities for supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator is responsible for effective implementation of supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Coordinator has responsibility, recipients may delegate implementation to other campus offices; the Department acknowledges that one individual alone may not be able to fulfill all duties if only a single Coordinator is designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex stereotyping and gender-based harassment within sexual harassment framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender-based harassment, which may include verbal, nonverbal, or physical aggression, intimidation, or hostility based on sex or sex-stereotyping (not involving conduct of a sexual nature), may constitute sex discrimination and sexual harassment that a school must address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include repeated sabotaging of female graduate students' laboratory experiments by male students. The regulations do not preclude sex-stereotyping theories from underlying unwelcome conduct that constitutes sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual exploitation covered when it meets sexual harassment definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual exploitation is addressed to the extent that it constitutes sexual harassment as defined in §106.30; the §106.45 grievance process applies to all formal complaints alleging sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sexual exploitation meets one of the prongs of the sexual harassment definition, it is subject to the grievance procedures in §106.45.
